documents.title: Declaration of Principles Concerning Activities Following the Detection of Extraterrestrial Intelligence
documents.issuer: IAA SETI Committee; adopted by the IAA and IISL
documents.summary: The original post-detection protocols. The discoverer should verify that extraterrestrial intelligence is the most plausible explanation before any public announcement, alert the other parties to the Declaration and national authorities, then notify the IAU Central Bureau for Astronomical Telegrams, the UN Secretary-General (under Article XI of the Outer Space Treaty) and a list of international scientific bodies. Confirmed detections are to be disseminated openly, with data shared and permanently archived, and the relevant radio frequencies protected through the ITU. Principle 8 states that no reply should be sent until appropriate international consultations have taken place. Principle 9 commits the IAA SETI Committee to continuing review and to setting up an international post-detection committee.
documents.notes: Approved in April 1989 by the IAA Board of Trustees and the Board of Directors of the International Institute of Space Law. Endorsed over the following three years by COSPAR, the IAU, URSI Commission J and the IAF. Replaced by the 2010 Declaration. This copy was printed from the IAA SETI Committee website (iaaseti.org) in September 2026.

documents.title: Cover letter from the IAA SETI Committee on the 1989 Declaration and the proposed Position Paper
documents.issuer: John Billingham (Chair), with co-chairs Iván Almár and Jill Tarter
documents.summary: A one-page letter summarising how the 1989 Declaration was adopted and endorsed. It records that the Declaration was sent in July 1992 to SETI researchers and organisations with a request to endorse it, and that the Committee had assembled a special post-detection committee under Principle 9. It also introduces the Position Paper that expands Principle 8 into a decision process for sending a reply.
documents.notes: Written on IAA SETI Committee letterhead from the SETI Institute, Mountain View. The PDF was created in 2003.

documents.title: A Decision Process for Examining the Possibility of Sending Communications to Extraterrestrial Civilizations: A Proposal
documents.issuer: IAA SETI Committee subcommittee led by Michael Michaud
documents.summary: An IAA Position Paper proposing an international process for deciding whether and how to send a communication to an extraterrestrial civilisation, whether in reply to a detection or in its absence. It reviews the science of SETI, sets out the issues raised by transmitting from Earth, and proposes that a Declaration of Principles on sending communications be developed.
documents.notes: Endorsed by the IAA Board of Trustees and the IISL Board of Directors. Sent by the IAA in September 1996 to the 63 member nations of COPUOS. Presented to COPUOS in June 2000 by Jill Tarter. This copy was printed from iaaseti.org in September 2026.

documents.title: Declaration of Principles Concerning the Conduct of the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence
documents.summary: A streamlined replacement for the 1989 Declaration, in eight principles. It adds a commitment to transparent searching and responsiveness to the media, and says there is no obligation to disclose verification work while it is under way. The Rio Scale is recommended for conveying the significance of candidate signals. Confirmed detections go to the public, the scientific community, the UN Secretary-General and the IAU. The Declaration keeps data archiving and ITU frequency protection, refers to a Post-Detection Task Group, and says signatories will not respond to a confirmed signal without first seeking the guidance and consent of a broadly representative international body such as the United Nations.
documents.notes: Unanimously adopted at the annual meeting in Prague on 30 September 2010. Replaced by the 2026 Update.

documents.title: Declaration of Principles Concerning the Conduct of the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (SETI) – 2026 Update
documents.issuer: International Academy of Astronautics; prepared by the IAA SETI Committee Post-Detection Task Group (chair: Michael Garrett)
documents.summary: The current protocols, rewritten for a search that now spans many kinds of technosignature and for a media environment shaped by social media and AI. Its eight principles cover handling candidate evidence, communicating during verification, reporting a confirmed detection, archiving and data access, data and frequency protection, a standing Post-Detection Sub-Committee, replying to a detection, and ethical and legal considerations. New provisions include steps to protect the safety of researchers, a right for individuals to decline media engagement, prompt disclosure when a candidate is ruled out, peer-reviewed verification reports, and archiving in at least two geographically separate repositories.
documents.notes: Prepared by the IAA SETI Committee's Post-Detection Task Group, chaired by Michael Garrett, with Kathryn Denning, Les Tennen and Carol Oliver. Developed in 2022–2025 with wide community consultation, approved by a vote of the Committee that closed on 31 January 2026, and adopted by the IAA Board of Trustees as an IAA Position Paper in spring 2026. This is the version published by the IAA, dated 1 June 2026. It replaces the 2010 Declaration.

documents.title: IAA Press Release 26/01: IAA adopts updated Declaration of Principles for SETI
documents.summary: The public announcement of the 2026 Update, described as the first major overhaul of the protocols in over 15 years and the product of consultation with more than 350 SETI researchers and practitioners. It highlights technosignatures beyond radio, protection of researchers, and managing viral rumours and hoaxes, and restates that any reply is a decision for all of humanity. Next steps are a permanent Post-Detection Sub-Committee, lodging the Declaration with the UN, and a technical presentation at IAC 2026 in Türkiye.

documents.title: The Rio Scale
documents.issuer: Iván Almár and Jill Tarter; IAA SETI Permanent Committee
documents.summary: An ordinal scale from 0 to 10 for rating the significance of any public claim of evidence for extraterrestrial intelligence, modelled on the Torino asteroid-impact scale. The value is RS = Q × d, where Q combines the class of phenomenon, the type of discovery and the distance, and d is the assessed credibility. It is meant to be revised as a claim is investigated. The 2010 Declaration recommends it for explaining candidate signals to non-specialists.
documents.notes: Proposed at the 51st IAC in Rio de Janeiro in October 2000. Adopted by the Committee in 2002; Revision 1.2 accepted in Bremen in 2003. A revised Rio Scale 2.0 was presented to the Committee in 2017. This copy was printed from iaaseti.org in September 2026.

documents.title: The San Marino Scale
documents.issuer: Iván Almár; IAA SETI Permanent Committee
documents.summary: The counterpart to the Rio Scale for transmissions from Earth. It rates the potential exposure of a deliberate transmission or reply on a scale of 1 to 10, as SMI = I + C, where I measures signal intensity relative to the Sun's background at the same frequency and C reflects the information content. It gives the debate over messaging to extraterrestrial intelligence (METI) a common measure.
documents.notes: Proposed in San Marino in March 2005 at the 6th World Symposium on the Exploration of Space and Life in the Universe. Endorsed and adopted by the Committee in Hyderabad in September 2007. This copy was printed from iaaseti.org in September 2026.

documents.title: Revising the SETI Post-Detection Protocols for the 2020s and Beyond: A Report on Work in Progress
documents.issuer: C. Oliver, K. Denning, L. I. Tennen, M. A. Garrett
documents.summary: The first public report from the task group set up in 2022 to revise the 2010 Declaration. It traces the protocols from 1989 and explains why revision is needed: social media and repeated false alarms have changed how information moves, and technosignature searches at Breakthrough Listen, the SETI Institute, FAST and elsewhere have grown in scale and scope, drawing in researchers who may not see themselves as working on SETI.
documents.notes: Presented at the 74th International Astronautical Congress, Baku, 2–6 October 2023. Copyright the authors; released to the IAF to publish.

documents.title: Draft Revised Declaration of Principles Concerning the Conduct of SETI (version 1 October 2024)
documents.issuer: IAA SETI Committee Post-Detection Task Group (chair: Michael Garrett)
documents.summary: The first full draft of the revised Declaration, presented at IAC 2024 in Milan. It introduces the technosignature framing, the balance between timely public information and the safety of individual scientists, and the plan to supplement the Declaration with Best Practices Guidelines and a Code of Conduct that can be updated regularly.
documents.notes: Presented to the IAA SETI Committee meeting on 16 October 2024 and in session A4.2 of IAC 2024.

documents.title: Comparison of the 2010 Declaration and the October 2024 draft
documents.issuer: IAA SETI Committee Post-Detection Task Group (chair: Michael Garrett)
documents.summary: The October 2024 draft annotated to show its lineage. Significant changes from the 2010 Declaration are marked in green, and wording brought back from the 1989 Declaration is marked in blue. Useful for seeing which parts of the original protocols the revision deliberately restored.
documents.notes: Circulated with the draft for the 2024 consultation.

documents.title: The Future of the SETI Post-Detection Protocols: Progress Towards Revisions
documents.issuer: L. I. Tennen, K. Denning, C. Oliver, M. A. Garrett
documents.summary: Reports the task group's progress after Baku, including further community consultation and proposed text. It sets out the model the revision followed: timeless Principles in the spirit of the 1989 Declaration, supplemented by Codes of Conduct and Best Practices that can be updated as circumstances change. It places the work alongside the 2024 NASA and IAU/Kavli meetings, the SETI Post-Detection Hub at St Andrews, and the IISL working group on SETI and the Law.
documents.notes: Presented at the 75th International Astronautical Congress, Milan, 14–18 October 2024. Copyright the authors; released to the IAF to publish.

documents.title: Feedback process for the 2024 update of the Post-Detection Protocols
documents.issuer: Michael Garrett for the IAA SETI Committee Executive
documents.summary: The consultation plan agreed in Milan. Committee members, including the heads of Breakthrough Initiatives and the SETI Institute, would comment first, followed by the wider SETI community (the IAA SETI community list of about 325 people) and groups such as the Order of the Octopus. Feedback would be anonymous, by email or online survey. The final draft would go to a member vote decided by a simple majority, followed by notification of IAA officials and a public presentation at IAC 2025.
documents.notes: Presented at the IAA SETI Committee meeting, IAC 2024, Milan.

documents.title: Draft Revised Declaration of Principles – 2026 Update (version 25 September 2025)
documents.issuer: IAA SETI Committee Post-Detection Task Group (chair: Michael Garrett)
documents.summary: The draft that came out of the 2025 consultations and was presented to the Committee at IAC 2025 in Sydney. It is close to the final text. After one more round of comments from members, a version dated 27 November 2025 was put to the vote.
documents.notes: Presented at the IAA SETI Committee meeting on 1 October 2025.

documents.title: Feedback process for the 2025 update of the Post-Detection Protocols
documents.issuer: Michael Garrett for the IAA SETI Committee Executive
documents.summary: Reports on the consultations held in spring 2025 (Committee members) and summer 2025 (the wider community, including the Order of the Octopus, the SETI Post-Detection Hub and the IISL SETI and Law Working Group). About 20% of those invited responded, and over 70% rated the draft 8 or more out of 10. It sets out the path to adoption: a final round of member comments, an anonymous online vote decided by a simple majority, submission to the IAA Board of Trustees, and a public presentation at IAC 2026.
documents.notes: Presented at the IAA SETI Committee meeting, IAC 2025, Sydney.

documents.title: SETI Post-Detection Protocols: Progress Towards a New Version
documents.issuer: M. A. Garrett, K. Denning, L. I. Tennen, C. Oliver
documents.summary: The third task group paper, presenting the results of the structured consultation and a new draft of the revised Declaration at IAC 2025 in Sydney. It explains that the aim was to keep the lasting values of the earlier documents while making them fit twenty-first-century science, media and public engagement, and that the protocols are a living document that will need continued refinement.
documents.notes: Presented at the 76th International Astronautical Congress, Sydney, 2025. This copy is the penultimate version (11 September 2025), not the final text submitted to the IAF.

documents.title: Declaration of Principles vote (2025–2026): summary report
documents.issuer: Michael Garrett, IAA SETI Committee Chair
documents.summary: The result of the Committee's vote on the 27 November 2025 version of the 2026 Update, held on the Helios secure voting system from 2 December 2025 to 31 January 2026. Of 91 eligible members, 57 voted (63% turnout): 53 in favour (93%), 1 against and 3 abstentions. Ballots were anonymous.

documents.title: Update to the IAA SETI Committee on adoption of the 2026 Update
documents.issuer: Michael Garrett, IAA SETI Committee Chair
documents.summary: Explains what happened after the Committee vote. The task group and the IAA executive turned the approved text into a formal IAA Position Paper, replacing references to the SETI Committee with references to the IAA and adopting the standard Position Paper format, with no substantive changes. The IAA Board of Trustees approved it in spring 2026. Next steps include the Post-Detection Sub-Committee, best-practice work, presentation to the UN and circulation to observatory directors.
documents.notes: Phone numbers and private Dropbox and Zoom links have been removed from this copy.

documents.title: The History of the IAA SETI Permanent Committee – The Early Years
documents.issuer: Lori A. Walton and Stéphane Dumas
documents.summary: The first in a series of papers on the Committee's history, covering the introduction of extraterrestrial intelligence to the IAA in 1965, the first CETI review session at the 1972 IAC in Vienna, and the founding of the Committee in 1974 and its work up to 1979. It describes the Committee's mandate, including its long-standing role in drafting protocols for detection, verification, announcement and response.
documents.notes: Presented as the John Billingham Cutting Edge Lecture at the 66th IAC, Jerusalem, 2015. Copyright the International Astronautical Federation; reproduced with the permission of the IAF and the author. This copy is marked as a draft.

documents.title: The History of the IAA SETI Permanent Committee – 2000 to 2009

It also covers the debate over 'active SETI', the Rio and San Marino scales, and the search programmes of the period.

documents.title: Terms of Reference for IAA Committees, including the SETI Committee
documents.summary: New Terms of Reference for all IAA committees, including the SETI Committee, are expected to be adopted soon by the IAA Board of Trustees. They will set out each committee's scope, officers, membership and procedures, including the election of new members. The document will be added here once it has been adopted.

documents.title: The History of the IAA SETI Permanent Committee – 1980 to 1989
documents.summary: The second paper in the history series, covering the 1980s. It describes how the Committee studied the legal, political and social implications of detecting an extraterrestrial signal and drafted the Declaration of Principles Concerning Activities Following the Detection of Extraterrestrial Intelligence, approved by the IAA Board of Trustees and the Board of Directors of the International Institute of Space Law in 1989. It also covers the roughly thirty SETI searches of the decade, NASA's SETI programme and the founding of the SETI Institute.
documents.notes: Presented at the 70th International Astronautical Congress, Washington DC, 2019. Copyright the International Astronautical Federation; reproduced with the permission of the IAF and the author.

documents.title: The History of the IAA SETI Permanent Committee – 1990 to 1999
documents.summary: The third paper in the history series, covering the 1990s, which it calls a pivotal and turbulent decade for SETI. The Committee continued to disseminate the 1989 Declaration of Principles and worked on the IAA Position Paper on whether and how to respond to a detection. The paper also covers the growing public interest at the end of the decade: the first confirmed extrasolar planets, the claim of possible fossil life on Mars, the film Contact, false claims of detections and the launch of SETI@home.
